purpose: Reconciles the blockAssetsOnDemand toggle with WP 6.9's new default of loading separate core block styles on demand in classic themes: on 6.9+ the toggle becomes an opt-out (OFF forces combined wp-block-library loading via should_load_separate_core_block_assets -> __return_false at priority 10) while pre-6.9 cores keep the legacy opt-in filter unchanged.
riskRationale: The class-main.php logic is small, correct, and verified against WP core source, but the commit also bundles the entire composer dev-dependency tree (~4,700 files / ~525K lines: phpunit, phpcs, wpcs, brain/monkey, patchwork, mockery, etc.) into the tracked vendor/ directory, violating the documented composer-release workflow and risking dev tooling leaking into the release ZIP. The 6.9+ opt-out is also registered globally rather than classic-theme-only, and the default-OFF value silently reverts WP 6.9's on-demand default on fresh installs.
breakingChanges: On WP 6.9+, setting blockAssetsOnDemand OFF now forces combined wp-block-library loading (opt-out semantics), reverting core's new on-demand default for classic themes on default-config installs.

The commit adds the entire dev-dependency vendor tree (phpunit, php_codesniffer, wpcs, brain/monkey, patchwork, mockery, etc.) to the tracked vendor/ directory, which previously contained only production packages.

text: The core fix in includes/class-main.php is technically sound: the function_exists('wp_load_classic_theme_block_styles_on_demand') guard matches the existing 6.9 feature-detection pattern, the priority-10 __return_false correctly overrides core's priority-0 __return_true for classic themes, and the pre-6.9 elseif branch preserves the legacy opt-in behavior byte-for-byte. However, the commit is heavily contaminated: it ships ~4,700 dev-only vendor files (~525K lines) contrary to AGENTS.md's production-only vendor workflow, and the opt-out filter is registered globally rather than scoped to classic themes, so block themes currently depend on an accidental core filter-ordering coincidence to stay on separate assets.

reasoning: The PHP fix is sound and mergeable on its own, but the commit must be stripped of the dev-dependency vendor tree via composer release before merge, and the 6.9+ opt-out should be guarded with wp_is_block_theme() so block themes keep WP 6.9's separate-assets default. Both fixes are straightforward and mechanical.

message: Registering __return_false at priority 10 correctly overrides core's priority-0 __return_true (apply_filters resolves to the last callback), so the opt-out deterministically forces combined loading on classic themes, and a single filter also cascades to should_load_block_assets_on_demand. Verified against the WP 6.9/7.0 core source and matches the canonical 'Load Combined Core Block Assets' workaround plugin.

The function_exists('wp_load_classic_theme_block_styles_on_demand') version guard mirrors the existing wp_should_output_buffer_template_for_enhancement guard pattern used at lines 357/370 of the same method, and timing is satisfied because setup_hooks() runs from the Main constructor at plugin load, before core's wp_load_classic_theme_block_styles_on_demand() runs during init/wp_default_styles.
The pre-6.9 elseif branch preserves the original should_load_block_assets_on_demand opt-in filter exactly, so sites on WP 6.2-6.8 experience zero regression from the restructure.

The PR commit adds ~4,738 files / ~525K insertions to the tracked vendor/ directory — the ENTIRE dev-dependency tree (phpunit, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, mockery, nikic/php-parser, sebastian/*, etc.), flipping the installed.php 'dev' flag from false to true. This directly violates AGENTS.md ('run composer release ... git add vendor/ (include the production-only vendor)') and contradicts the PR description's stated ~7-file scope. .distignore excludes only the phpcs-related dirs, so phpunit, brain, mockery, antecedent, etc. would leak into the release ZIP if any packaging path skips the composer --no-dev prune, and master was already cleaned of exactly this churn in prior commits.
suggestion: Run composer release (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader) and recommit vendor/ so only production packages (voku/html-min, matthiasmullie/minify, woocommerce/action-scheduler) are tracked; also add the remaining dev-only namespaces (phpunit, sebastian, brain, mockery, hamcrest, antecedent, myclabs, phar-io, staabm, theseer, nikic) to .distignore as a safety net.
suggestionCode:
composer release
git add vendor/  # production-only deps only

message: The opt-out filter is registered unconditionally on 6.9+, so it also applies to block themes, where core registers should_load_separate_core_block_assets -> __return_true via _add_default_theme_supports() at the same priority 10 but later (during after_setup_theme) and therefore wins. Block themes currently stay on separate on-demand assets only by this registration-order coincidence; if core ever changes the priority or ordering, block-theme sites would silently regress to the large combined wp-block-library stylesheet. Some reviewers assess block themes are already affected today since the setting defaults to false, making the behavior actively regressive — either way, it is undocumented and fragile.
suggestion: Scope the opt-out to classic themes with an explicit wp_is_block_theme() check (matching the canonical workaround plugin) so block themes keep core's separate-assets default by intent, not by filter-ordering luck.

message: blockAssetsOnDemand defaults to false (line 176), so on every fresh WP 6.9+ classic-theme install with default settings the plugin registers should_load_separate_core_block_assets -> __return_false, actively reverting WP 6.9's documented on-demand block-styles performance improvement and forcing the combined wp-block-library stylesheet. This inverted semantics (opt-in on <6.9, opt-out on 6.9+) is a silent behavior change for existing users after upgrade.
suggestion: Make a deliberate, documented product decision: either default blockAssetsOnDemand to true on 6.9+ so the plugin embraces core's on-demand default, or keep OFF and explicitly document (readme/changelog) that default-config 6.9+ installs intentionally revert to combined loading.

message: The toggle description ('Only load block CSS and JavaScript when blocks are actually used on the page. Requires WordPress 6.8 or later.') is now inaccurate on WP 6.9+, where on-demand is the core default for classic themes and the toggle only matters as an opt-out (OFF forces combined loading). A user toggling it ON on 6.9+ sees no behavior change, which is misleading.
suggestion: Update the description to reflect that on WP 6.9+ classic themes load block assets on demand by default and the toggle acts as an opt-out (disable it to force the combined wp-block-library stylesheet), while on WP 6.8 enabling it loads block assets only when used.

message: The correctness of the fix depends on a subtle, undocumented priority contract (10 must beat core's priority-0 __return_true for classic themes but lose to core's later-registered same-priority 10 for block themes), and no automated test covers the new version-gated branching (4 combinations: <6.9/6.9+ x toggle ON/OFF). This logic can silently regress.
suggestion: Add a comment documenting the priority-0 (core) vs priority-10 (plugin) contract and registration-timing requirement, and add a brain/monkey-based unit test (already in require-dev) asserting the registered filter name, callback and priority for each combination under mocked function_exists/wp_is_block_theme.
